title: Eval-harness runner for baseline vs quantized comparisons (profile publish gating)
creator: Jonas Weber
content:
Background / why
Quantization Profile Library v1 requires a repeatable, reviewable way to compare baseline (fp16/bf16) vs a proposed quantized profile (int8/int4) across prompt sets before publishing a profile to the library.

Today we can run eval-harness manually on a single model endpoint, but we do not have:
- a standardized job type that runs paired baseline vs quantized variants with identical prompts
- a single report artifact (human + machine readable) suitable for PR review
- a gating signal we can wire into the “publish profile” workflow (pass/fail + reasons)

This ticket adds an eval-harness runner/job type that:
1) runs baseline + quantized back-to-back (or interleaved) using the same promptset(s)
2) computes deltas + statistical checks
3) stores results as an immutable artifact with a stable identifier
4) posts/links the report to the profile publish PR/workflow so reviewers can sign off

Links
- Confluence: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/quantization-profile-eval-harness-integration.json
- Confluence: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/profile-validation-quality-gates.json
- PR (eval-harness): sources/github/eval-harness/pr_642_quantization_profile_comparison_job.json

Scope
- Add a new eval-harness job type: quant_profile_comparison
- Standardize config schema for the job (baseline ref, quantized ref, promptsets, metrics)
- Produce output artifacts:
  - comparison_summary.json (machine-readable; used for gating)
  - comparison_report.md (human-readable; used for review)
  - per-prompt trace bundle (optional flag; stored for debugging)
- Upload artifacts to the existing eval artifact store (S3/GCS depending on env) with deterministic paths
- Emit a “gating signal” (pass/fail + top failures) that can be consumed by the profile publish pipeline

Non-goals (v1)
- Replacing the full manual review process (humans still approve)
- Automatically selecting prompt sets (the calling workflow will specify promptset ids)
- Automatic rollback/disable (handled by runtime/platform + SRE workstream)

Proposed job config (v1)
- job_type: quant_profile_comparison
- baseline:
  - model_ref: (e.g., redwood://model-registry/llama-3.1-70b-instruct@baseline)
  - endpoint/region: optional override for where to run
- quantized:
  - model_ref OR (model_ref + quant_profile_id + quant_profile_version)
  - required: quant_profile_id, quant_profile_version in report metadata even if resolved by runtime
- promptsets:
  - list of promptset ids (e.g., qlib_core_v1, qlib_json_mode_v1, qlib_tool_calling_v1)
  - sampling settings (max_prompts per set, random_seed)
- execution:
  - concurrency, retries, timeout
  - request params: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, json_mode/tooling flags
- metrics:
  - output format validity (JSON schema checks, tool-call envelope checks)
  - exact/near match on gold outputs where available
  - LLM-as-judge win-rate (optional; off by default for initial library gating)
  - safety/blocked rate deltas (if safety classifier enabled)
- gating:
  - thresholds by promptset (e.g., json_validity >= 99.5%, tool_call_success >= 99.0%)
  - global max regression (e.g., -0.5% absolute on key success metrics unless exception filed)

Result format (comparison_summary.json)
- metadata: baseline_ref, quantized_ref, quant_profile_id/version, promptsets, commit SHA, run id, timestamps
- aggregates per promptset:
  - baseline_metrics, quant_metrics
  - delta (quant - baseline)
  - statistical notes (n, confidence intervals when applicable)
- gating:
  - pass: true|false
  - failing_checks: list of strings
  - top_regressions: list of strings

Storage conventions
- Artifact root: evals/quantization-profiles/{quant_profile_id}/{quant_profile_version}/{run_id}/
- Always write a “latest” pointer file per profile version for convenience, but keep all runs immutable:
  - evals/quantization-profiles/{quant_profile_id}/{quant_profile_version}/latest.json -> contains run_id + artifact URIs

Integration points
- Profile publish workflow (registry/publish pipeline) should:
  - call this job with the candidate profile + baseline reference
  - block publish on pass=false
  - attach comparison_report.md link to the profile publish PR (or at minimum include artifact URLs in the publish request response)

Acceptance criteria
- A single command (or CI job) can run baseline vs quantized comparisons with a pinned seed and produces the standard artifacts.
- comparison_summary.json contains all fields required for downstream gating (pass/fail + failures) and is stable across reruns given same seed + prompts.
- Report is linkable from the profile publish workflow (URL or artifact ID), and is easy for reviewers to read.
- Runner handles common failure modes gracefully:
  - partial endpoint failure -> retries; if still failing, mark run as failed with reasons
  - baseline/quant mismatch in model params -> fail fast with a clear error
- Basic unit tests + an integration test that exercises the job with a small promptset.

Implementation notes / decisions
- We run baseline + quantized requests in an interleaved order per prompt to reduce drift from time-varying backend behavior.
- We record the effective runtime-resolved quant_profile_id/version in the request metadata so the report can’t be ambiguous (important when the quantized ref is “model@latest”).
- For JSON-mode and tool-calling promptsets, gating defaults to format validity / tool-call success rather than free-form similarity scoring (matches feedback from early tool-calling regressions).

Rollout
- Behind feature flag in eval-harness job registry: enable for Applied ML and perf/evals first.
- First consumers: int8 profiles for initial model list; int4 comparisons only after qlib_json_mode_v1 and qlib_tool_calling_v1 promptsets are available (tracked elsewhere).

Open questions
- Do we require LLM-as-judge for any promptsets in v1, or keep it manual-only until we have calibration? (Current: optional, off by default.)
- Should we store per-prompt raw outputs by default? (Current: off by default; enable via --store-traces for debugging to manage cost/PII risk.)

2024-11-12 (Jonas Weber): Please ensure report captures effective quant_profile_id/version resolved by runtime (we’ve been burned by “latest” ambiguity). Also include n per promptset + seed in metadata.

2024-11-14 (Selene Huang): For MVP, prioritize output-format validity and tool-call success deltas; we can add judge-based scoring later. Also add a clear section listing “top failing prompts” with prompt ids so we can reproduce quickly.
2024-11-19 (Olivia Grant): Implemented quant_profile_comparison job skeleton + config parsing. Added interleaved execution mode. Working on summary JSON + markdown report templates.

2024-11-22 (Priyanka Bose): Request: include calibration notes pointer if available in profile metadata; even a free-text field in report metadata is helpful for review context. (Ok if pulled from publish request inputs.)
2024-11-26 (Olivia Grant): Added artifact uploader paths under evals/quantization-profiles/{profile}/{version}/{run}. Added latest.json pointer. Added --store-traces option for per-prompt outputs.

2024-12-02 (Olivia Grant): Hooked gating evaluation: thresholds configurable per promptset. Fail-fast for incompatible request params between baseline/quant legs. Added integration test using tiny promptset fixture.
2024-12-04 (Jonas Weber): Reviewed report output. Ask: include a single-line “GATING: PASS/FAIL” header at top of markdown plus failing checks list for quick scanning in PR review.
2024-12-06 (Olivia Grant): Addressed report header + quick-scan summary. Opened PR: sources/github/eval-harness/pr_642_quantization_profile_comparison_job.json
2024-12-11 (Mateo Alvarez): Confirmed request metadata includes resolved quant profile id/version tag from runtime; this will help when we’re comparing on mixed hardware pools.
